body: [{"streamId":"01a1ae78-295f-755c-a1d0-713966cb565d","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1ae78-295f-755c-a1d0-713966cb565d\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022RecordExportTests no longer fails intermittently with \\u0027The process cannot access the file ...coanda.db because it is being used by another process\\u0027 on macOS, Linux, or Windows, because nothing in the test process still holds a home\\u0027s coanda.db open when a test reads that file whole to show it unchanged.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022The pull request names the two opens of coanda.db that refuse each other, with the file and line of each at the commit the branch starts from, and the evidence for that pair: a reproduction, or a listing of open handles (for example lsof) taken while the read is refused.\u0022,\u0022Before the fix, the pull request reports an attempt to reproduce the failure on this Mac, with each command and how many runs it took. The attempt includes at least 100 runs of RecordExportTests alone and at least 10 runs of the full suite, because xUnit runs one class\\u0027s tests one at a time and the suspected trigger comes from other classes running in parallel. If the failure does not reproduce, the pull request says so and fixes only the pair the code shows.\u0022,\u0022Once an in-process daemon (RunningDaemon) has been disposed, no SQLite connection to its home\\u0027s coanda.db is left open in the process, so the home\\u0027s lock is never released while the daemon\\u0027s connections remain. A new test reads a home\\u0027s coanda.db whole straight after disposing a daemon on that home and passes on both CI legs, and the pull request says whether that test failed on the Windows leg before the fix.\u0022,\u0022After the fix, RecordExportTests passes 100 consecutive runs of the class and 10 consecutive runs of the full suite on this Mac, and the pull request gives the commands and the results.\u0022,\u0022No test is skipped, retried, wrapped in a retry loop, or given a longer wait; no existing assertion changes; and no new call to the process-wide SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools is added.\u0022,\u0022dotnet build --configuration Release succeeds with warnings as errors, and dotnet test --configuration Release --no-build passes on both CI legs.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## Why\\n\\nA verification run on this Mac of a change that touches no export code failed one test of 2,114: RecordExportTests.A_rebuild_refuses_when_the_records_last_event_is_not_the_one_the_export_names_and_changes_nothing, with System.IO.IOException \\u0027The process cannot access the file .../coanda-tests/\\u003Cid\\u003E/coanda.db because it is being used by another process\\u0027, thrown from SafeFileHandle.Open. The same message appeared earlier on the Windows CI leg in RecordExportTests (PR #69, main after #71). PR #74 (bc8dce2c) hardened daemon.json but did not reach the coanda.db case. It happens on macOS, so it can be diagnosed locally.\\n\\n## What the code shows at 2bdefd1\\n\\n- Nothing opens coanda.db with FileShare.None. The only .NET FileStream opens of it are \\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/NodeHome.cs:203\\u0060 (FileShare.ReadWrite, only when the file is first created) and the test\\u0027s whole-file read, \\u0060File.ReadAllBytes\\u0060 in \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060 at \\u0060tests/Coanda.Tests/Daemon/RecordHomes.cs:224\\u0060. Not every open goes through \\u0060OwnerOnly.Open\\u0060; that read does not.\\n- The other side is most likely a SQLite connection. The daemon\\u0027s store connects with \\u0060Data Source={databasePath}\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Store/StoreConfiguration.cs:32\\u0060), so Microsoft.Data.Sqlite pools its connections process-wide. \\u0060RunningDaemon.DisposeAsync\\u0060 (\\u0060src/Coanda.Daemon/Api/DaemonHost.cs:354\\u0060) disposes the host and then releases the home lock; nothing closes the pooled connections, so they stay open on the home\\u0027s coanda.db after the daemon is gone.\\n- On macOS, flock and fcntl locks on the same file do conflict, even within one process: a fcntl write lock on a byte range, which SQLite takes, refuses the shared flock with LOCK_NB that .NET takes for a read. This was checked on this Mac with a two-descriptor probe. On Linux the two kinds are independent. On Windows a FileShare.Read open is refused whenever SQLite holds the file open for writing, idle or not.\\n- \\u0060SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools()\\u0060 runs in \\u0060RecordExport.cs:81\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs:63\\u0060 and \\u0060:97\\u0060, \\u0060RecordHomes.cs:115\\u0060, and \\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:260\\u0060. It closes every idle pooled connection in the test process, including a disposed daemon\\u0027s on another test\\u0027s home. Closing the last connection to a record in write-ahead-log mode checkpoints it and takes an exclusive lock on coanda.db, which is when a concurrent whole-file read is refused. Pool pruning can close them too.\\n- In RecordExportTests, the failing test (\\u0060RecordExportTests.cs:425\\u0060) is the only one that reads a home\\u0027s files whole (\\u0060:436\\u0060, \\u0060:440\\u0060) after an in-process daemon ran on that same home (\\u0060:431\\u0060).\\n\\nRead \\u0060RecordHomes.Files\\u0060, \\u0060RunningDaemon\\u0060, \\u0060StoreConfiguration.Configure\\u0060, and the failing test first. \\u0060RecordExport.cs\\u0060, \\u0060RecordRebuild.cs\\u0060, \\u0060HomeLock.cs\\u0060, and \\u0060OwnerOnly.cs\\u0060 explain the lock and the existing pool handling.\\n\\n## Direction\\n\\nThe smallest fix that ends the problem is for \\u0060RunningDaemon\\u0060 to close the connections in its own pool, for its own connection string and not process-wide, before it releases the home lock. That keeps \\u0060HomeLock\\u0060\\u0027s promise that an export or rebuild never runs beside a daemon, and it covers every test that inspects a home after a daemon, not only this one. A fix confined to the test would leave the next such test with the same race.\\n\\n## Non-goals\\n\\nNo change to the export file format, the rebuild\\u0027s behaviour, or the record\\u0027s schema. The existing \\u0060ClearAllPools\\u0060 calls stay as they are. No change under
